svg.text: JWT: a concert wristband, kept in an httpOnly cookie
Concepts 4–5 · the wristband is signed, not secret · the browser attaches it, not JavaScript code
Wristband = JWT: three pieces of base64url text, joined by dots
example payload from Concept 4 · payload and signature cut short with …
A JWT's header and payload are JSON objects
written without spaces, so they start with {", and
in base64url that start becomes eyJ.
A long text starting with eyJ: most likely
a JWT, and anyone can read what's in it.
account number in the users table, as text
session number in the sessions table (Concept 7)
when the wristband was made (seconds since 1970)
anyone can read it, without a key:
so no email, no name, certainly no password
in .env; empty, short, or still the
example text: the server won't run
Kept in the browser as two cookies (the login answer: two Set-Cookie headers)
stores them, then attaches them itself
the page's JavaScript can read it
XSS: the wristband is stolen, then used
sent in your name; the defenses:
SameSite, the origin check, and CORS
